title: Crocker Art Museum receives major gift of 23 artworks from collector Gordon W. Bailey
summary: The Crocker Art Museum in Sacramento CA has received a substantial gift of 23 artworks from scholar and collector Gordon W. Bailey. Known for his advocacy of untrained artists, Bailey's thoughtfully curated gift features works by both self-taught and trained artists. All of the artists are new to the Crocker. “We are honored to join the outstanding institutions that have received donations from Mr. Bailey. It is critical that museums reflect and engage the communities they serve, and Mr. Bailey’s gifts strengthen the Crocker’s ability to do this in an exceptional way," said Agustín Arteaga, PhD, Mort and Marcy Friedman Director & CEO The Crocker, founded in 1885, is the oldest museum in the West

title: Christie's reveals major new highlights for inaugurating Abu Dhabi fine-art auction
summary: Christie's reveals additional highlights for its landmark auction MAWASIM: 20 Years of Modern and Contemporary Middle Eastern Art. Bringing together 70 works spanning nine decades, the offering traces the richness and diversity of artistic production across the Middle East and North Africa. Taking place on 1 November at The Abu Dhabi EDITION, the sale marks Christie's first fine-art auction in Abu Dhabi and continues the house's longstanding engagement with the region. title: Musée du Louvre unveils landmark 17th-century Spanish polychrome sculpture survey
summary: 'Sculpting Colour', presented at the same time and in the same space as the exhibition 'Zurbarán (1598–1664)', and with collaboratively designed scenography by Nathalie Crinière, invites visitors to take a close, comparative look at 17th-century Spanish sculpture, presented here for the first time in France. Through an exceptional, carefully chosen selection of 23 of the finest sculptures, all on loan thanks to an exclusive partnership with Spain's Museo Nacional de Escultura in Valladolid, visitors will discover the striking, singular art of Spanish sculpture in the 1600s. title: RISD announces inaugural Movement Lab Symposium
summary: Rhode Island School of Design presents its inaugural Movement Lab Symposium from October 14–16, 2026. The three-day event will highlight interdisciplinary research conducted by Movement Lab fellows via panel discussions, performances, screenings, and speakers on RISD’s campus, as well as an exhibition at the nearby Jamestown Arts Center . The Movement Lab Fellowship offers post-graduate artists and scholars the opportunity to focus on independent creative research that advances the study of movement into uncharted territory. title: Hauser & Wirth Los Angeles presents Jack Whitten's 1980s works in 'The Numinous'
summary: Following the late artist’s critically acclaimed 2025 retrospective at The Museum of Modern Art, New York, Hauser & Wirth presents ‘The Numinous,’ an exhibition of Jack Whitten’s paintings and works on paper from the 1980s, at its Downtown Los Angeles gallery. The exhibition focuses on a pivotal and still underexamined period in Whitten’s six-decade career, where technical innovation and spiritual inquiry came together with new force. After a 1980 house fire forced an extended pause in his practice, Whitten returned with renewed urgency. Testing and pushing acrylic paint to new effects, he began to treat the medium as a dense, malleable material—something that could be cut, layered and collaged like ‘a skin.’ Another turning point came in 1983, when The Studio Museum in Harlem presented a survey of Whitten’s work from 1970–1980, organized by

title: Christie's reveals $100M 'Heroes and Lovers' collection spanning 500 years of art history
summary: Christie's announced Heroes and Lovers—a collection of nine ambitious masterpieces representing pinnacles of spirituality, sensuality and raw human emotion across 500 years of art history. The collection spans sublime Old Master paintings and sculpture through to icons of Modernism with works by Tilman Riemenschneider, Cornelis Cornelisz. van Haarlem, François Le Moyne, Jean-Honoré Fragonard, Édouard Manet, and four examples by Pablo Picasso. Collectively, these works create a visual map of extreme and intimate moments of the human experience—exploring notions of passion, morality, courage and connection, as captured by six of the most influential artists dating from the fifteenth through the twentieth centuries. Together, the collection is estimated in the region of $100 million. Seven

title: Interactive toy survey 'Architectural Construction Kits 1890-1990' opens at MAK Vienna
summary: Starting on 7 October, the MAK will present the major interactive exhibition ARCHITECTURAL CONSTRUCTION KITS 1890–1990, transforming several of the museum’s rooms into an interactive play area for children aged four and up, as well as adults. Around 70 architectural construction kits from the years 1890 to 1990, many presented in the form of fully assembled models, showcase the vast diversity of historical toys. The basis for the exhibition is the private collection of graphic designer Claus Krieger, comprising around 150 items. Of the once countless toy construction kits—between 1880 and 1960, some 900 companies produced them in the German-speaking world alone—only a few are still manufactured today. While most children today grow up with Lego, there was once a wealth of materials: artificial brick, wood, and metal were used, alongside long-forgotten materials like Galalith and even rubber. title: Thaddaeus Ropac announces representation of British painter Denzil Forrester
summary: Over more than four decades, Denzil Forrester (b. 1956) has developed a painting practice rooted in the vital sounds and energy of London’s dub and reggae scene in the early 1980s, giving form to rhythm, movement and emotion through line and colour. Translating music techniques of sampling, mixing and looping into visual terms, he creates bold, dynamic compositions that are rooted in tradition while remaining distinctly his own. I have long admired Denzil’s work. Just as his artistic forebears drew from the scenes of music and nightlife, he too has an outstanding ability to distil atmospheric energy, movement, together with communal emotions of joy, longing or fear. His paintings are among the most enthralling and distinctive of his generation, and having shown Denzil’s work in our group exhibition Artists I Steal From, curated by Alvaro Barrington in 2019, we are excited to now represent him. — Thaddaeus Ropac The gallery announced that the first solo exhibition

title: Reba McEntire opens her fashion vault for benefit sale
summary: Julien’s Auctions will present “The Reba Collection,” a special benefit sale taking place live in person at Musicians Hall of Fame & Museum at the Historic Nashville Municipal Auditorium on Friday, October 23 starting at 10 a.m. CT / 11 a.m. ET. Celebrating the iconic career of global superstar Reba McEntire, this auction features an extraordinary array of her personal items, with all proceeds generating critical support and awareness for The Reba McEntire Fund to benefit various local and national non-profit initiatives. To explore the auction catalog and register to bid, visit Julien’s Auctions. Oklahoma’s own McEntire is a multimedia entertainment icon whose dynamic career spans music, television, film, theater, retail, and hospitality. A Country Music Hall of Fame member and 2018 Kennedy Center Honors recipient, she has earned more than 50 award wins, including honors from the ACM, AMA, CMA, GRAMMY, GMA Dove and People’s Choice. title: Brooklyn Museum exhibits historic gift of modern European masterworks from Pearlman Collection
summary: This fall, the Brooklyn Museum opened Cézanne to Modigliani: Gifts of Modern Art from the Pearlman Collection. The exhibition, which follows LACMA’s presentation on view in early 2025, showcases more than fifty modern European works from the late nineteenth to mid-twentieth century, drawn from the renowned collection of Henry and Rose Pearlman. Featuring paintings, sculptures, and works on paper, Cézanne to Modigliani celebrates the transformative gift of this stellar collection to the Brooklyn Museum, LACMA, and MoMA. The Pearlman Foundation’s decision to entrust the stewardship of these treasures to be shared across three institutions is the ultimate manifestation of their family’s generosity and commitment to sharing their prized artworks with a wide public. title: RM Sotheby's flagship UK sale at London's Peninsula Hotel to offer spectacular selection of cars
summary: RM Sotheby’s flagship London auction will return on 31 October 2026, taking its traditional position on the eve of the RM Sotheby’s London to Brighton Veteran Car Run. Following the success of last year’s £24-million sale, the auction will be held for the third successive year at The Peninsula London in Belgravia. This year’s sale is shaping up to be another wonderful event with incredible cars spanning over 125 years of automotive history. Very much the market’s car of the moment, many eyes will be on the 1988 Ferrari F40 The Ferrari F40. title: Tate Britain captures the raw energy of 'The 90s' in landmark art and fashion survey
summary: Tate Britain has opened the first exhibition to explore the art, photography and fashion of the 1990s, a decade synonymous with possibility, optimism and an audacious spirit. The 90s: Art and Fashion explores this period’s surge of creative energy, shaped by its opportunities and challenges. Featuring nearly 70 artists, photographers and designers, from the Young British Artists (YBAs) to Alexander McQueen, the show spotlights the emergence of this generation of exciting and diverse artistic talent that reshaped Britain’s cultural identity. Drawing on curator Edward Enninful OBE’s experience of the decade, The 90s brings together over 100 photographs, paintings, sculptures and garments to re-evaluate one of the most transformative moments in British art. Following the gritty economic uncertainty of the 1980s, the 1990s saw the emergence of a resourceful new generation of young talent in Britain. The exhibition opens by exploring their taste for imperfection and realness

title: Washington County Museum of Fine Arts announces Executive Director transition
summary: The Washington County Museum of Fine Arts announced that Executive Director Sarah J. Hall will be stepping down from her position, effective December 18, 2026, to become Director of Galleries at the Pittsburgh Cultural Trust. Hall has led WCMFA since July 2020, bringing nearly 30 years of experience in museums, exhibitions, collections, and public programming to the role. During her six-year tenure, she guided the Museum through the unprecedented challenges of the COVID-19 pandemic, expanded online programming, strengthened and diversified the exhibition program, helping to build the reputation of the Museum as a Mid-Atlantic destination and raise regional awareness of its high-quality collection and programs. Among the notable exhibitions presented during Hall’s tenure were Bernini & the Roman Baroque: Masterpieces from the Palazzo Chigi in Ariccia, the museum's first exhibition of Old Master paintings in nearly 60 years. title: Singapore Art Museum launches nine-month rotating collection display 'The Present is Unstable'
summary: Singapore Art Museum presents SAMCollection: The Present is Unstable, approaching collection display through a dynamic format that considers how works in the museum’s collection reflect the changing conditions of our world today. The exhibition will host a rotating roster of works over its nine-month run. As works are replaced and reconfigured, shifting relationships within and between them emerge, creating a dynamic space where new readings and conversations surface over time. The exhibition opens with works that consider movement as a fundamental condition of our experience and how embodiment and looking propose ways to witness the world, situate ourselves, and move through our environment. title: Galleria d'Arte Maggiore g.a.m. brings Giorgio Morandi dialogues to Paris
summary: The enduring relevance of Morandi’s work, as articulated in the opening text of the 1987 exhibition at the Hôtel de Ville de Paris, provides the starting point for this exhibition. Although forty years have passed since that landmark exhibition, realized in collaboration with the City of Bologna, the text written by Franco Solmi brings us back to a querelle that remains open: the search for the secret of an art that has traversed — and continues to traverse — the great transformations of yesterday and today without being diminished by them. title: Tomma Abts expands into site-specific architecture with major Rotunda commission at Fridericianum
summary: Tomma Abts’s paintings and drawings reflect an ongoing investigation of form, color, and pictorial space. Working primarily in acrylic and oil, she develops her paintings in a slow, step-by-step process in which diverse forms and nuanced color palettes coalesce into dynamic pictorial compositions. At the invitation of the Fridericianum, Tomma Abts is broadening her artistic practice for the first time to create a site-specific interior wall painting that responds to the distinctive architecture of the Rotunda on the second floor. Beneath a fan-shaped glass roof, a spacious atrium is enclosed by a gallery that curves along one side. Drawing on the space’s distinctive architectural features and light conditions, the artist develops a composition of four geometric forms: a circle, a square, an ellipse, and a rhombus. title: T206 Honus Wagner steps up to the plate in Heritage Fall Sports Catalog Auction
summary: A card widely considered the Holy Grail of baseball cards and featuring one of the greatest players in the history of the game will race into the spotlight when it is offered in the Heritage Fall Sports Catalog Auction Oct. 23–25. No card has captivated collectors like the 1909-11 T206 White Border Sweet Caporal 150/25 Honus Wagner PSA Authentic (Restored) that is in play in this auction. This card, featuring the Hall of Famer known as “The Old Dutchman,” appeared briefly in 1909, but production quickly stopped, adding a measure of rarity that launched it into the top tier of desirability. title: Heritage Auctions launches The Walking Dead Universe Auction
summary: Heritage Auctions will present The Walking Dead Universe Auction, a Showcase auction featuring costumes, props and set pieces from the world of AMC’s hit series The Walking Dead. Taking place October 30, the sale offers fans and entertainment memorabilia collectors unprecedented access to acquire beloved pieces of television history directly from the archives of the network that created the series, which became a pop culture phenomenon and launched a thriving television franchise. The Walking Dead follows survivors confronting the undead and the human conflicts that emerge after civilization collapses. Its costumes and props help tell that story, establishing the identities of its central characters and the deteriorated world around them. title: Warhol's American West leads Heritage's October 22 Prints & Multiples Auction
summary: John Wayne, Geronimo and Annie Oakley share the stage with ceremonial objects and a familiar five-cent coin in Andy Warhol’s Cowboys and Indians, a vivid portrait of the American West as both history and legend. Offered as a complete portfolio of ten screenprints with its original box, the 1986 suite leads Heritage Auctions’ October 22 Prints & Multiples Signature® Auction, a sale that pairs some of the artworld’s most recognizable names with discoveries for collectors at a range of price points. “Warhol’s iconic Cowboys and Indians portfolio brings together so many of the collecting passions that define Heritage, from Western art and Hollywood to American history and even coins,” says Aviva Lehmann, Heritage’s Deputy Chairman of Fine Art. “Offering the complete portfolio gives us an extraordinary opportunity to connect collectors

title: Ben Uri spotlights postwar refugee art colony in new exhibition
summary: Ben Uri announced the exhibition, The Abbey Art Centre as Postwar Refuge, 1946–56, marking the simultaneous publication of The Abbey Art Centre in postwar London 1946–1956, eds., Jane Eckett, Ian McLean and Sheridan Palmer (Routledge), this autumn. The exhibition unfolds the remarkable story of the Abbey Art Centre, a cosmopolitan art colony established at New Barnet in 1946 by charismatic artist, gallerist and world art collector, William Ohly (1883–1955). A crucible of creativity on London’s northern edge, the Abbey was a postwar haven for stateless Jewish refugees, as well as artists from Australia, Britain and continental Europe. title: The Sixth New Museum Triennial: The Outside Expands opens February 4, 2027
summary: The New Museum today announced the artist list for the 2027 New Museum Triennial: The Outside Expands on view February 4 through May 16, 2027. Founded in 2009, the New Museum Triennial is the only recurring international exhibition in New York City devoted to early-career artists from around the world. Now in its sixth iteration, the 2027 New Museum Triennial will feature 36 artists and collectives from 34 different countries—the widest international representation in a New Museum Triennial to date—and will be the first Triennial to take place within the newly opened OMA-designed expansion. The 2027 Triennial is co-curated by Vivian Crockett, Allen and Lola Goldring Curator at the New Museum, and Isabella Rjeille, Curator at MASP—Museu de Arte de São Paulo Assis Chateaubriand, with Thalia Stefaniuk, Curatorial Assistant, and Taeyi

title: Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts announces 2026-2027 Collider Fellows
summary: Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts today announced its 2026-2027 class of Collider Fellows. The nine-month Fellowship gives six artists the time, space, and support to pursue creative research and experimentation, free from conventional commission requirements such as a final product or project. The Fellows receive studio space, both at Lincoln Center and at Collider collaborator Onassis ONX, the Onassis Foundation’s global platform for art and advanced technologies; financial stipends; artistic and administrative support from Lincoln Center staff; and regular opportunities to collaborate with one another. This year's cohort brings together artists working across immersive media, performance, film, sound, installation, and digital art. title: White Cube unveils major modern and contemporary presentation for Art Basel Paris
summary: White Cube returns to Art Basel Paris with a group presentation of works by artists including Georg Baselitz, Alexander Calder,​ Helen Frankenthaler, Louise Giovanelli, Antony Gormley, David Hammons, Marguerite Humeau, Suleman Aqeel Khilji, Ibrahim Mahama, Giorgio Morandi and Francis Picabia, among others.
